jobs.description: About Deel | Global HR Solutions for Hiring & Management​ Special Offer Get 3 months free of PEO* Claim offer About Deel Work with the world Work with the world Millions of people working for the world’s best companies, no matter the location? Sounds like the future. We make managing a global team easy, so businesses don’t need to think twice. Trusted by 40,000+ companies from startups to enterprise 175 STORIES Read about real results The future of Global HR, a platform you can use today Deel equips teams with the tools, features, and guidance they need in a single platform to eliminate hiring and management borders. Businesses and teams can work together easier than ever and gain access to new opportunities. How Deel came about After graduating from MIT in 2014, Co-Founders Alex Bouaziz (CEO) and Shuo Wang (CRO) noticed a trend among their friends: they couldn’t get high-paying jobs they were highly qualified for due to visa issues and local labor laws in other countries. It was an apparent problem. The duo started Deel to make a change for people everywhere by empowering companies to eliminate hiring borders—so anyone, anywhere in the world, could access new opportunities. At Deel, we’ve always been our first customer, which helps keep us poised to break new ground for our customers. As the company and team grew, we tackled more problems we faced, from onboarding employees to automating tedious processes. Now, Deel's evolved beyond just hiring to simplify every aspect of building a global team. Meet our founders Alex Bouaziz (CEO & Co-Founder) Alex Bouaziz is the CEO and co-founder of Deel, the all-in-one HR platform for global teams. Founded in 2019, Deel’s technology helps companies simplify every aspect of managing an international workforce, from culture and onboarding, to local payroll and compliance. In just under four years, the company has grown to 4,000+ team members worldwide in over 100 different countries and raised over $600 million in funding. It has 35,000-plus customers, including Shopify, Nike, and Klarna. Alex grew up in Paris and graduated from Technion and then MIT with a Masters in Civil and Environmental Engineering. Prior to Deel he co-founded investment fund Sarona Ventures. In 2020 he was featured on Forbes’ 30 Under 30 Finance list. Outside of Deel, Alex enjoys cheering on Paris Saint-Germain Football Club. Shuo Wang (CRO & Co-Founder) Shuo Wang is the Chief Revenue Officer and Co-founder of Deel, an all-in-one HR platform for global teams. Shuo drives Deel's revenue and led the company in scaling from $1-$100M ARR in under 20 months. Deel simplifies every aspect of managing an international workforce, from culture to payroll and compliance. The company has grown to 4,000+ team members across the globe in 100+ countries, raised over $600M in funding, and has 35,000+ customers including Shopify, Nike, and Klarna. Prior to Deel, Shuo co-founded Aeris Cleantec and served as CTO until its acquisition by iRobot. Shuo holds a BS degree in Mechanical Engineering and Robotics from MIT, where she met Deel's CEO, Alex Bouaziz. Shuo is passionate about inspiring more women to get involved in software development, product management, and marketing. jobs.title: Compliance Verification FAQ
jobs.description: Understanding Compliance Verification at Deel – Deel Skip to main content Deel Request a Demo Blog About Submit a request Deel For business Account Access Articles in this section Understanding Compliance Verification at Deel The Deel Referral Program: Earn Rewards for Sharing Deel Protecting your business and everyone you pay Paying people across borders relies on trust. Wherever Deel moves money on your behalf, we verify the business and the people behind it, so your payments move through a network where identities are confirmed and bad actors are kept out. That protects your payments, your workers, and your account . For you, this means you don't need to stand up a compliance function of your own; Deel does the verification work so you don't have to. Once your business is verified for a given product, you won't need to redo that check to keep using it. If you add a new regulated product later, or expand into a new entity, we'll let you know exactly what's needed at that point. Most reviews finish within one business day. We also know this is the least interesting part of getting started. So we've kept it to what's actually required, told you upfront what to have ready, and made it clear where to get help if something doesn't fit your situation. This page walks you through what to expect, why we ask for it, and where to go if you have questions along the way. In this Article 1. Why we verify every customer 2. What to expect before you start 3. Documents you'll likely need 4. Why we ask for personal identification 5. Verifying your workers 6. When we ask for more information 7. How we protect your information 8. Where to get help Frequently Asked Questions Compliance verification process 1. Why we verify every customer Before you can pay a contractor, or move money through Deel, we need to confirm who you are and who owns your business. This isn't an internal Deel policy, it's a legal requirement. Deel's regulated entities are licensed financial and payment institutions , which means we're bound by anti-money laundering (AML), anti-terrorist financing laws and know your customer (KYC) laws wherever we offer regulated financial services. If you're only using unregulated services, you likely won't need to complete this process at all, even if you pay Deel for those services through the platform. That's because the trigger isn't paying Deel; it's Deel moving money on your behalf. Requirements scale with what you're using Deel for and which country or jurisdiction you're operating in. There are three levels: Full verification (what the rest of this page covers): applies where Deel moves money or employs on your behalf: contractor payments, Global Payroll with Treasury (where payroll is paid out through Deel, not just calculated), US Payroll, and PEO. A lighter check: applies to Employer of Record (EOR) and Contractor of Record (COR), where Deel employs or contracts workers on your behalf. For these, we verify your business itself (name, registration, address, industry) and screen it for sanctions and adverse media. We'll also ask for your expected monthly transaction volume, but we don't identify or verify your beneficial owners, directors, or controlling officer. The submitter must still confirm their own identity and provide a Proof of Authority. No verification: applies to unregulated services like HR tools, applicant tracking, IT management, or payroll calculation on its own, without Deel moving the money. Note: the level is set by the products enabled on your entity, not the ones you actively use. If a money-movement product like Treasury or contractor payments is switched on for an entity that only uses EOR, that entity will be asked for full verification. If that's not what you intended, ask your account team to disable the unused product. 2. What to expect before you start Once you've submitted everything, our team usually completes the review within one business day. If anything in the submission doesn't match our records or needs clarification, we'll come back to you and the process will take longer. Because regulated services cannot be activated until verification is complete, we recommend starting as soon as possible. Key details to keep in mind before you dive in: Who needs to submit it: Regulators want this information to come from you, not a third party, so it should be submitted by someone within your business who holds operational authority Key People Required: You will need details for: Submitter: The person completing and submitting this verification on your business's behalf. Must provide proof of authority, unless they're already listed as your Key Decision-Maker or a director. Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) : Anyone owning 25% or more of the company. Key Decision-Maker: At least one person with real day-to-day authority over the business, someone who could say yes or no to major decisions on your company's behalf. Depending on your structure, that might be a founder, owner, CEO, or managing director (functional leads, like a Head of HR, generally do not qualify). We don't collect this in Canada or Australia. Directors: Required in select jurisdictions (e.g., UK, EEA, Canada, Australia, Singapore). What can vary: exact requirements differ by country and entity type. This page covers the general picture; your account team can walk you through specifics for your situation. 3. Documents you'll likely need Here's what most businesses need to have on hand. The exact list can vary a bit by country and the Deel products you're using: Entity formation documents (articles of incorporation or organization, or your country's equivalent). A tax registration number (EIN or your country's equivalent). Proof of your registered business address* (see the note below, there's often nothing extra to submit for this). Proof of Authority : a document confirming that whoever is submitting or signing for your business is authorized to do so, for example, a board resolution or a signed lett
